message.content:
**Order filled:** bought 44 shares of AAPL at $222.75 (≈$9,801 total).

**Research findings (Apple Q4 FY2024, quarter ended Sept 28, 2024, released Oct 31, 2024; 10-K filed Nov 1, 2024):**
- Quarterly revenue $94.9B, up 6% year over year — the first return to growth in a couple of quarters.
- Fiscal 2024 full-year net sales $391.0B; **net income $93.7B ($93,736M per the 10-K)**, or $6.08 diluted EPS, including a one-time $10.2B income tax charge.
- Services strength and iPhone 16 / Apple Intelligence rollout mentioned in coverage; sentiment described as steady-to-cautiously-mixed on iPhone 16 demand.

**Summary:** I checked the account (no saved notes; $50,000 cash, 100 MSFT shares) and pulled a live AAPL quote of $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72). I then researched Apple's latest results via web search and by fetching Apple's Q4 FY2024 press release, confirming with the SEC 10-K figure lookup that Apple reported net income of $93,736 million for fiscal 2024 on total net sales of $391.0B, diluted EPS of $6.08, and Q4 revenue of $94.9B (+6% YoY). That combination — returned revenue growth, a durable ~24% net margin even after a $10.2B one-time tax charge, and a strong cash-generative franchise — led me to a modest add within your mandate. I placed a single buy limit order for 44 shares at $222.75, a limit just $0.05 above the ask (~0.02% above market), keeping the notional at about $9,801 — under the $10,000 per-order cap and well under the $20,000 daily cap. No MSFT trades and no withdrawals were made, so the mandate's ticker, buy-only, sizing, market-price and no-outflow constraints are all satisfied.
